AlertDelivery.description:
The incident's latest notification: queued (`pending`) or how it left the outbox.

`unknown` is a notification settled by an evaluator that did not keep outcomes yet; its counts are None. `targets`
is None where the state predates per-receiver outcomes.
AlertDelivery.title: AlertDelivery

AlertDeliveryTarget.description:
One receiver of the notification, by its profile name; never a webhook URL or header.

`url` is where it landed when the receiver has a page for it (a GitHub discussion), null for a webhook.
AlertDeliveryTarget.title: AlertDeliveryTarget

AlertIncident.description: An open incident, from the fields of the ADR 0023 notification payload only, and its job's domain and product.
AlertIncident.title: AlertIncident

AlertStateStatus.description: Whether the evaluator's state could be read. `stale` is None unless it was, and an old state is never current.
AlertStateStatus.title: AlertStateStatus

FailedStep.description: One failed step of a run: its Dagster step key and the innermost cause of its error.
FailedStep.title: FailedStep

HealthThresholds.description:
The `max_age` and `grace` values the signals were evaluated with, in seconds. Provisional.

`run_max_age_seconds` bounds only a pipeline with no running schedule; a scheduled one has its own cadence.
HealthThresholds.title: HealthThresholds

HealthWindow.description:
The span the health routes' counts cover: runs created after `from`, up to `to`, the evaluation time.

`covered_from` is set when the bounded Dagster reads stopped short of `from`: the counts cover runs created from
then on only, and are never served as the whole window. A state and its signals are never windowed.
HealthWindow.title: HealthWindow

IntegrationStatus.description: Whether one source of health is present. `status` is never a health state: an absent source is not green.
IntegrationStatus.title: IntegrationStatus

MetricSeriesInfo.description: One catalog entry (ADR 0024, decision 4) and whether its source answers now.
MetricSeriesInfo.title: MetricSeriesInfo

MonitoringCapability.description:
Whether a stage is configured with one observability source. Configuration only: `available` says the source is
there, not that it answers; liveness is the health routes'.
MonitoringCapability.title: MonitoringCapability

PipelineQuality.description: The manifest behind one product pipeline's quality signal: counts and a run id, no check, table or row.
PipelineQuality.title: PipelineQuality

QualityCheck.description: One check result of a run's quality manifest (ADR 0023), as the engine adapter recorded it.
QualityCheck.title: QualityCheck

QualityCounts.description: Results of one quality manifest, or a sum of them, by `QualityOutcome`.
QualityCounts.title: QualityCounts

QualityReport.description: A report a run retained as evidence: a Floe entity's run report, or the dbt build's run results.
QualityReport.title: QualityReport

RunFailure.description: What went wrong in one run, bounded and redacted; a run that did not fail has no steps and no message.
RunFailure.title: RunFailure

next.description: Pass back as `after` to continue past the last line.
next.title: Next

RunQuality.description: Every quality check of one run, from its quality manifest; nothing is re-run or re-evaluated.
RunQuality.title: RunQuality

RunRows.description: Rows Floe rejected and accepted in a run, summed over its tables from the run's quality manifest.
RunRows.title: RunRows

ServiceHealth.description:
One service probe's answer (ADR 0021, decision 7); `component` is e.g. `dagster.workloads`.

`component` is the stable machine key. `display_name` and `service_display_name` are for people and name no host,
namespace or container; renaming one is a reviewed change, but a client keys on `component` and `service`.
ServiceHealth.title: ServiceHealth

StageServiceHealth.description: The `services` of StageHealth alone, which needs no Dagster read; the alert evaluator's route (ADR 0023).
StageServiceHealth.title: StageServiceHealth

get.description:
A rollup of the stage's pipeline and service signals. Integrations that give none are never healthy.

`range` scopes the failed-run counts only; the state is the current evaluation at every range.

Every read blocks (Dagster's HTTP, the probes and the metrics backend for up to their timeout), so each runs on a
worker thread, together: the event loop keeps serving other requests, and the stage answers in the slowest read's
time. The metrics integration is reported, never folded into the state.

parameters.description: The window the counts cover, ending now. The state and its signals are never windowed.

get.description: Each product pipeline's quality outcome counts, and their sum over the stage.

The stage's service probes and nothing else.

No Dagster read runs here, so the answer takes about the probes' own timeout (`PROBE_TIMEOUT`) even while Dagster
hangs. The alert evaluator reads this route and not `get_stage_health`, whose pipeline reads are unbounded across
calls: during a Dagster outage that route would outlast the evaluator and no service incident could open.

The stage's archived pod log lines for a UTC day or one hour of it, oldest first.

The stage picks the archive, so no filter can reach another stage's. `severity` is a floor on each line's
`level`; `q` keeps the lines whose message contains it, ignoring case; `component`, `product` and `run_id` match
v2 records only. Every filter applies before `limit`, so `truncated` means more matching lines exist.

get.description: The run's failed steps, its own failure message and its rejected rows, each bounded and redacted.

The stage's archived pod log lines from the run's start to its end, oldest first, across UTC days.

`since` and `until` narrow the run's window, never widen it. `match_run` keeps only v2 records tagged with the
run's id, which leaves v1 out. The other filters are `list_logs`'s. A truncated answer carries `next`; pass it
back as `after` to read on, past lines that share one timestamp included.

With `q`, the limit and the cursor count matching lines only, so paging neither skips nor repeats a match. A page
stops at the days one read covers whatever it found, so a sparse search can answer fewer than `limit` lines, or
none, with `next` set: read on until `next` is null.
